newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES RELEASE GOALTENDER CASEY, THREE OTHERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES RELEASE GOALTENDER CASEY, THREE OTHERS.

text.p: The St. Louis Blues announced Tuesday that four players, including veteran goaltender Jon Casey, accepted contract buyouts and were released.
Defenceman Trent Yawney, left wing Sergio Momesso and right wing Rob Pearson were the other players who accepted buyouts.
"These roster moves will allow us more flexibility with our younger players, who will compete for those positions next season," said new Blues general manager Larry Pleau.

The 35-year-old Casey played 15 games as a backup to Grant Fuhr last year and was 3-8 with a 3.39 goals-against average. He has a career record of 170-157-55 with 16 shutouts in his 11-year NHL career.

Casey, who was the goaltender on the Minnesota North Stars team that reached the 1991 Stanley Cup final, enjoyed his best year in 1993-94 when he went 30-15-9 with four shutouts and a 2.88 goals-against average for the Boston Bruins.
Yawney played 39 games for the Blues last year and was plus-two with two assists. Momesso had just one goal in 40 games and Pearson scored one goal in 18 games for the Blues last year.
